questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{2{e}^{x}}{(1+{e}^{x})^{3}},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

find the cumulative distribution function $F(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
The cumulative distribution function of a continuous random variable $X$ is the function $F(x)$ defined by

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(x) & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{2{e}^{t}}{(1+{e}^{t})^{3}}\,\text{d}t \\  & ={-\frac{1}{(1+{e}^{t})^{2}}|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{(1+{e}^{x})^{2}}+1 \\  & =1-\frac{1}{(1+{e}^{x})^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}2(-x+4),\, & 3\le x\le 4 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<3 \\ h(x),\, & 3\le x\le 4 \\ 1,\, & x>4.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the function $h(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $3\le x\le 4,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<3 \\ {\int }_{3}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & 3\le x\le 4 \\ 1, & x>4\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{3}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{3}^{x}2(-t+4)\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={8t-{t}^{2}|}_{3}^{x} \\  & =-{x}^{2}+8x-15.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<3 \\ -{x}^{2}+8x-15, & 3\le x\le 4 \\ 1, & x>4.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\frac{{e}^{-|x/3|}}{6},\,x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{x/3}}{2},\, & x<0 \\ h(x),\, & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

Find the function $h(x).$
questions.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that involves an absolute value, the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{{e}^{t/3}}{6}\,\text{d}t, & x<0 \\ {\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{t/3}}{6}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-t/3}}{6}\,\text{d}t, & x\ge 0\end{aligned}
$$

Let's compute the integrals.

- If $x\le 0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{x}\frac{{e}^{t/3}}{6}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{t/3}}{2}|}_{-\infty }^{x} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{x/3}}{2},\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{t/3}}{6}\,\text{d}t & ={\frac{{e}^{x/3}}{2}|}_{x=0} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

- If $x>0,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-t/3}}{6}\,\text{d}t & =-{\frac{{e}^{-t/3}}{2}|}_{0}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{{e}^{-x/3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

As a result, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\infty }^{0}\frac{{e}^{-t/3}}{6}\,\text{d}t+{\int }_{0}^{x}\frac{{e}^{-t/3}}{6}\,\text{d}t & =\frac{1}{2}+(-\frac{{e}^{-x/3}}{2}+\frac{1}{2}) \\  & =1-\frac{{e}^{-x/3}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}\frac{{e}^{x/3}}{2}, & x<0 \\ 1-\frac{{e}^{-x/3}}{2}, & x\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the cumulative distribution function

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<0 \\ \frac{x}{6}-\frac{{x}^{3}}{1458}, & 0\le x\le 9 \\ 1, & x>9,\end{aligned}
$$

find $P(1<X\le 3).$
questions.worked_solution:
We can perform this computation as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(1<X\le 3) & =P(X\le 3)-P(X\le 1) \\  & =F(3)-F(1) \\  & =(\frac{3}{6}-\frac{{3}^{3}}{1458})-(\frac{1}{6}-\frac{{1}^{3}}{1458}) \\  & =\frac{230}{729}.\end{aligned}
$$

questions.problem:
Given that the random variable $X$ has the probability density function

$$
f(x)=\{\begin{aligned}-\frac{2}{9}x+\frac{8}{9},\, & 1\le x\le 4 \\ 0,\, & \text{otherwise}\end{aligned}
$$

its cumulative distribution function is 

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0,\, & x<1 \\ h(x),\, & 1\le x\le 4 \\ 1,\, & x>4\end{aligned}
$$

where $h(x)=${{field-1}}.
questions.worked_solution:
Since our random variable $X$ has a probability distribution function $f(x)$ that is strictly positive only for $1\le x\le 4,$ the cumulative distribution function takes the following form:

$$
F(x)=P(X\le x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ {\int }_{1}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t, & 1\le x\le 4 \\ 1, & x>4\end{aligned}
$$

For the given probability density function, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{1}^{x}f(t)\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{1}^{x}(-\frac{2}{9}t+\frac{8}{9})\,\text{d}t \\ \text{ } & ={(-\frac{1}{9}{t}^{2}+\frac{8}{9}t)|}_{1}^{x} \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}{x}^{2}+\frac{8}{9}x-\frac{7}{9} \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}({x}^{2}-8x+7) \\  & =-\frac{1}{9}(x-1)(x-7).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the cumulative distribution function is given by

$$
F(x)=\{\begin{aligned}0, & x<1 \\ -\frac{1}{9}(x-1)(x-7), & 1\le x\le 4 \\ 1, & x>4.\end{aligned}
$$
